html:
In the app

Guided mode’s lesson 17 is this chapter: it checks that the lesson’s tags are made, that S13_Mix exists, is called from MainRoutine and verifies, and then watches the line while you run it and ticks each result as it happens:

  • The kitchen makes a batch: Mix_Step goes through 3 (heat and mix) to 4 (ready)
  • A ready batch transfers to Supply_Tank while its inlet is open (Mix_PumpOut)
  • The carbonator holds its CO2: Carb_Press between 19 and 22 psi with soda going through
  • START on Tank_HMI after a STOP runs the kitchen again (Mix_Run)

Until now Supply_Tank has been filled from the plant supply header: open the inlet and soda arrives, as much as you like. A real filling line rarely works like that. The product is made a batch at a time in a mix kitchen beside the line and pumped across to a surge tank in front of the filler, which is what Supply_Tank becomes in this lesson. The kitchen is the Mix Tank of Level 11 with two supply totes, water on inlet A and cola syrup on inlet B, a carbonator after it, and a Process HMI to run it (chapter 14). Soda is made here, not bought: water and syrup at the 5 : 1 throw, then chilled and carbonated on the way to the filler.

Steps 1 to 12 do not change. Step 6 still opens the Supply_Tank inlet at the low float and closes it at the high float. What changes is where that inlet draws from: it is piped from the kitchen, and liquid only moves while the mix tank’s outlet pump runs. So step 13 has to have a batch ready whenever step 6 asks, and pump it across while the inlet is open. If it is late, step 11’s alarm bit 5 is the first to tell you, and step 6’s head-tank protection the second.

Place the kitchen

The kitchen stands to the right of the console. Place:

The mix kitchen

  • Supply Tote at x 1720, y 130, named Supply_A: Holds (units) = 20000. Water, a big tote: it lasts a long shift.
  • Supply Tote at x 1720, y 380, named Supply_B: Ingredient = Cola syrup; Holds (units) = 20000. Cola syrup: five parts of water go with each part of it, so it lasts five times as long as the water.
  • Mix Tank at x 2020, y 300, named Mix_Tank: Product (picked on the RECIPE page of its HMI) = Soda; Starts at (%) = 90; Pump A flow (units/s) = 150; Pump B flow (units/s) = 150; LO level probe (%) = 15; Panel and HMI: heater setpoint tag (a REAL the operator sets on the TEMP page) = Mix_Target_T; Recipe: A share the HMI aims for (%) = 83; Recipe: mixing time (s) = 8; Starts holding a finished batch: the start level made to the recipe A share and already mixed = ticked; Inlet A fed from = Supply_A; Inlet B fed from = Supply_B. Inlet A from Supply_A, inlet B from Supply_B; the heater setpoint tag is the one Tank_HMI writes; it starts at 90 % holding a finished batch, so the first transfer does not wait for a batch to be made.
  • Carbonator at x 2300, y 330, named Carbonator: Fed from = Mix_Tank; Starts at (psi) = 20. To the right of the tank, fed from Mix_Tank. It chills what goes through to 38 °F and dissolves CO2 in it; it starts at 20 psi, pressurised from the last shift.
  • Process HMI at x 2050, y 490, named Tank_HMI: Shows = Mix_Tank; Function keys F2–F6: other machines this terminal can switch to (names, comma-separated; F1 is Shows) = Supply_Tank, Case_Packer, Camera, Bottle_Feed; Heater setpoint tag (REAL; blank = the tank's own) = Mix_Target_T; START button tag (BOOL, pulsed while touched) = Mix_Start; STOP button tag (BOOL, pulsed while touched) = Mix_Stop; Running indicator tag (BOOL: lights START) = Mix_Run; Recipe A share tag (REAL, %) = Mix_Ratio; Recipe mixing time tag (REAL, s) = Mix_Time; Recipe carbonates tag (BOOL: 1 when the recipe takes CO2; the kitchen's CO2 rung reads it) = Mix_Carb; Carbonation key tag (BOOL: the key switch on the console; the MAIN page shows CARBONATION ON / OFF) = Carb_Key. In front of the tank, where the operator stands. Its START, STOP and Running tags are the kitchen’s own; its ratio, mixing time and carbonation tags take the RECIPE page’s values.

Then select Supply_Tank and set its Inlet fed from to Carbonator. The transfer line runs from the mix tank’s outlet pump through the carbonator and along a pipe rack at the back of the floor to the reservoir’s inlet. Guided mode’s Place the kitchen for me does all of this in one click.

The batch

One percent of Mix_Tank’s level is 20 units, and one pulse of a flowmeter is 20 units, so the room left to the HI probe (90 %) is 90 − Mix_Level pulses. A batch tops the tank up to HI: the water dose is the recipe’s water share of that room, counted on flowmeter A, and the syrup runs until HI. From an empty tank at the soda recipe’s 83 % water that is 75 pulses of water, 1500 units, and 300 of syrup: five to one. Then the batch is heated with a 2 °F band and mixed for the mixing time once it is up to temperature, and it is ready.

Why top up, and not wait for the tank to empty the way Level 11 does? Because the transfer is not up to the kitchen. Step 6 closes the inlet at the high float, whatever is left in the mix tank, and opens it again at the low float, ready or not. A kitchen that waits for an empty tank before it makes the next batch will sooner or later be half-way through one when the reservoir calls. Topping up the moment a transfer ends means a full, mixed batch is standing in the tank every time Supply_Tank asks, and what was left from the last batch is already at the recipe.

Add the JSR under step 15, above JSR(S3_Index), and write:

Tags this lesson needs

TagTypeKindDescription

Mix_RatioREALbase tagWater share of the batch, %: A SHARE on the RECIPE page
Mix_CarbBOOLbase tagThe recipe takes CO2 (1 for soda; set by the RECIPE page on Tank_HMI). The carbonator's CO2 valve only works while it is 1: juice, water and milk go through still
Mix_TimeDINTbase tagMixing time, s: MIX TIME on the RECIPE page

Mix_Auto_StartBOOLbase tagOne scan when the line starts: starts the kitchen too
Mix_StartBOOLbase tagSTART on Tank_HMI (pulsed by the touch screen)
Mix_RunBOOLbase tagThe mix kitchen is running (its own seal-in)
Mix_StopBOOLbase tagSTOP on Tank_HMI (pulsed by the touch screen)
Mix_MsDINTbase tagMixing time in ms (Mix_Time × 1000)
Mix_Lo_TREALbase tagBottom of the heater band: 2 °F under Mix_Target_T
Mix_StepDINTbase tagKitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer
Mix_HiBOOLalias of Local:12:I.Data.4Mix_Tank HI probe (90 %)
Mix_PumpOutBOOLalias of Local:6:O.Data.3Mix_Tank outlet pump: transfers to Supply_Tank
Mix_LevelINTalias of Local:11:I.Ch0DataMix_Tank level, 0-100 %
Water_LowBOOLalias of Local:10:I.Data.15Supply_A (water tote) at its low switch
Conc_LowBOOLalias of Local:12:I.Data.0Supply_B (syrup tote) at its low switch
Dose_PreDINTbase tagWater dose for this batch, in flowmeter pulses
Dose_ACOUNTERbase tagWater dose: flowmeter A pulses
Mix_PumpABOOLalias of Local:6:O.Data.1Mix_Tank pump A: water
Mix_FlowABOOLalias of Local:12:I.Data.1Mix_Tank flowmeter A: one pulse per 20 units
Mix_PumpBBOOLalias of Local:6:O.Data.2Mix_Tank pump B: syrup
Mix_LoBOOLalias of Local:12:I.Data.5Mix_Tank LO probe (15 %)
Mix_MixerBOOLalias of Local:6:O.Data.5Mix_Tank mixer
Mix_TempINTalias of Local:11:I.Ch1DataMix_Tank temperature, °F
Mix_HeatBOOLbase tagHeater wanted (latched under the band, unlatched at the setpoint)
Mix_ThermostatBOOLalias of Local:12:I.Data.6Mix_Tank high-limit thermostat (180 °F)
Mix_HeaterBOOLalias of Local:6:O.Data.4Mix_Tank heater
Mix_TimerTIMERbase tagMixing time at temperature
Mix_Empty_TTIMERbase tagLO uncovered this long: the tank is empty
Carb_PressINTalias of Local:11:I.Ch2DataCarbonator tank pressure, psi
Carb_CO2BOOLalias of Local:6:O.Data.6Carbonator CO2 inlet valve
Carb_KeyBOOLalias of Local:3:I.Data.13The carbonation key on the console, 1 turned to ON: the kitchen may carbonate
Carb_LampBOOLalias of Local:5:O.Data.10The amber CO2 lamp beside the key: carbonation enabled

The rungs

How it fits together

Rung 0 gives the recipe tags their defaults the first time: a REAL that nobody has set is 0, so 0 means “not set yet”: 100 °F, 83 % water, 8 s, and Mix_Carb latched, because soda takes CO2. Picking a product on Tank_HMI’s RECIPE page loads its recipe into the same tags. Rungs 1–2 are the kitchen’s own run circuit. It is separate from Line_Run because a kitchen often runs when the line does not (the first batch is made before the shift starts), and the operator at Tank_HMI must be able to stop it without stopping the line. The console’s Start starts both: rung 1 turns the rising edge of Line_Run into a one-scan start.

Rungs 3–4 turn the screen’s units into the program’s: seconds into milliseconds for the mixing timer, the setpoint into the bottom of the heater band. Rung 5 is power-up: a tank standing at HI holds a finished batch, so step 0 goes straight to 4. Rung 6 is the transfer: a ready batch, the kitchen running, and step 6’s inlet open. That one rung is the whole interface between the kitchen and the line.

Rung 7 starts a batch, either from empty (step 0) or as a top-up (step 4, the inlet closed, the tank below 80 %), and only while both totes are above their low switches. CPT works out the water dose from the room and the recipe in one expression; RES clears the counter; MOV goes to step 1. From here each output comes straight after the step that runs it: rung 8 runs pump A in step 1; rungs 9–10 dose the water, a CTU on flowmeter A whose preset is the tag Dose_Pre; rung 11 runs pump B in step 2, never past HI, and rung 12 ends the syrup at HI. Rung 13 runs the mixer in steps 3 and 4, only with the impeller covered; rungs 14–16 are the heater band and the heater, never past the high-limit thermostat; rungs 17–18 time the mix once the batch is up to temperature and make it ready. Rungs 19–20: if a transfer empties the tank, the sequence returns to 0 and starts again.

Rung 21 is the carbonator. Everything the transfer pumps across goes through it, chilled to 38 °F, and takes up CO2 according to the tank pressure, so 19 to 22 psi gives the 3.5 volumes of the soda recipe. The rung is an on-off band with a seal-in: under 19 psi the CO2 valve opens, and XIC(Carb_CO2) keeps it open until 22, where LES(Carb_Press,22) goes false and the valve shuts until the pressure falls under 19 again. XIC(Mix_Carb) in front of it is the recipe (only a product that takes CO2 is carbonated) and XIC(Carb_Key) beside it is the operator’s key on the console; rung 22 lights the amber CO2 lamp beside the key.

Run it

Run mode, Start. Put Mix_Step, Dose_A.ACC, Mix_Level, Mix_Temp, Carb_Press and Supply_Level in Quick Watch. Within a few seconds Supply_Tank falls under its low float, step 6 opens the inlet, and with the batch ready the outlet pump runs: the transfer line fills, Supply_Level climbs to 90 % and the inlet closes. Then Mix_Step goes to 1, the water doses, pump B tops up to HI, the heater and mixer run to 100 °F and eight seconds, and Mix_Step is 4 again long before Supply_Tank is back down at its low float. During a transfer Carb_Press saws between 19 and 22. On Tank_HMI, STOP stops the kitchen while the line keeps running, and START runs it again.

Try it: make the kitchen late

Press STOP on Tank_HMI, set MIX TIME to 60 s on the RECIPE page, press START and run for five minutes. Find the moment Supply_Tank reaches its low float while Mix_Step is still 3, and watch alarm bit 5 latch ten seconds later. Then put MIX TIME back to 8 s, and in rung 7 delete the top-up branch so the kitchen waits for an empty tank before it makes the next batch. Run again: how long before the same alarm? That is the reason for the top-up.

Try it: flat soda

Delete rung 21 and run. The carbonator starts at 20 psi, so the first transfers are fine, but each one takes some of the pressure and nothing puts it back. Watch Carb_Press fall and the Simulator Log start to report flat soda at the filler. Put the rung back. Then take LES(Carb_Press,22) out of it: the valve opens and seals itself in for good, the pressure climbs until the relief valve lifts. That is what the relief valve is for, and why every real band has its top as well as its bottom.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 0
rungs.comment: RECIPE DEFAULTS: a value of 0 means nobody has set it yet: the soda recipe, 100 °F, 83 % water (the 5 : 1 throw: five parts water to one of cola syrup), 8 s of mixing. Picking a product on Tank_HMI's RECIPE page loads its recipe into these tags

pred.q: Mix_Target_T is 0, Mix_Ratio is 0 and Mix_Time is 1. What does the rung do?
pred.a: Power reaches only part of the rung: Mix_Target_T is written, Mix_Ratio is written, Mix_Carb latches on and Mix_Time is not written (it keeps its value).

rungs.words: Each path is tested on its own: if Mix_Target_T (Batch temperature, °F: the setpoint on Tank_HMI (TEMP page)) equals 0.0, it puts 100.0 into Mix_Target_T; if Mix_Ratio (Water share of the batch, %: A SHARE on the RECIPE page) equals 0.0, it puts 83.0 into Mix_Ratio and latches Mix_Carb (The recipe takes CO2 (1 for soda; set by the RECIPE page on Tank_HMI). The carbonator's CO2 valve only works while it is 1: juice, water and milk go through still) on; if Mix_Time (Mixing time, s: MIX TIME on the RECIPE page) equals 0, it puts 8 into Mix_Time.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. EQU(Mix_Target_T,0.0) Equal asks: true when Mix_Target_T equals 0.0. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. MOV(100.0,Mix_Target_T) Move does: puts 100.0 into Mix_Target_T. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. EQU(Mix_Ratio,0.0) Equal asks: true when Mix_Ratio equals 0.0. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
      Path 1
      1. MOV(83.0,Mix_Ratio) Move does: puts 83.0 into Mix_Ratio. It writes every scan the rung is true.
      Path 2
      1. OTL(Mix_Carb) Output Latch does: latches Mix_Carb on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 3
    1. EQU(Mix_Time,0) Equal asks: true when Mix_Time equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. MOV(8,Mix_Time) Move does: puts 8 into Mix_Time. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Mix_Target_T = 0.0, to 100.0); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.
pats.think: a recipe card with numbered steps and one finger on it. Each rung only reads the line under the finger; when its line is done it moves the finger to the next number.
pats.watch: A rung further down that tests for the new step number sees it in this same scan. Rung order decides whether the next step starts now or next scan.

pats.why: Mix_Carb stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 1
rungs.comment: KITCHEN AUTO-START: one scan when the line starts, so the console Start starts the kitchen too
rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Mix_Auto_Start (One scan when the line starts: starts the kitchen too) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. ONS(Mix_Line_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Mix_Line_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. OTE(Mix_Auto_Start) Output Energize does: turns Mix_Auto_Start on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 2
rungs.comment: KITCHEN RUN: a seal-in of its own. START and STOP on Tank_HMI pulse Mix_Start and Mix_Stop, so the kitchen can run, or be stopped, without the line

pred.q: Mix_Start is off, Mix_Auto_Start is off, Mix_Run is off and Mix_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Mix_Run is off. None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: When either (Mix_Start (START on Tank_HMI (pulsed by the touch screen)) is on), (Mix_Auto_Start (One scan when the line starts: starts the kitchen too) is on) or (Mix_Run (The mix kitchen is running (its own seal-in)) is on) and Mix_Stop (STOP on Tank_HMI (pulsed by the touch screen)) is off, the rung turns Mix_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Mix_Start) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Start is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Mix_Auto_Start) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Auto_Start is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Mix_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Run is on.
  2. XIO(Mix_Stop) Examine If Open asks: true when Mix_Stop is off.
  3. OTE(Mix_Run) Output Energize does: turns Mix_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Mix_Run on, and Mix_Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 3
rungs.comment: RECIPE → MIX TIME: seconds on the screen, milliseconds for the timer preset
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung makes Mix_Ms (Mixing time in ms (Mix_Time × 1000)) = Mix_Time (Mixing time, s: MIX TIME on the RECIPE page) × 1000.
rungs.ltr: 1. MUL(Mix_Time,1000,Mix_Ms) Multiply does: makes Mix_Ms = Mix_Time × 1000.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 4
rungs.comment: HEATER BAND: the bottom of the band is 2 °F under the setpoint
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung makes Mix_Lo_T (Bottom of the heater band: 2 °F under Mix_Target_T) = Mix_Target_T (Batch temperature, °F: the setpoint on Tank_HMI (TEMP page)) − 2.0.
rungs.ltr: 1. SUB(Mix_Target_T,2.0,Mix_Lo_T) Subtract does: makes Mix_Lo_T = Mix_Target_T − 2.0. Every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 5
rungs.comment: POWER-UP: a batch left standing in the tank (up at HI) is ready to transfer
rungs.words: When Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 0 and Mix_Hi (Mix_Tank HI probe (90 %)) is on, the rung puts 4 into Mix_Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Mix_Step,0) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_Hi) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Hi is on.
  3. MOV(4,Mix_Step) Move does: puts 4 into Mix_Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Mix_Step = 0, to 4); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 6
rungs.comment: TRANSFER: a ready batch is pumped across, through the carbonator, whenever step 6 opens the Supply_Tank inlet. Step 6 is unchanged: it still opens the inlet at the low float and closes it at the high float; the kitchen just answers it

pred.q: Mix_Run is on, Supply_Inlet is on and Mix_Step is 4. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Mix_PumpOut is on.

rungs.words: When Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 4, Mix_Run (The mix kitchen is running (its own seal-in)) is on and Supply_Inlet (Supply_Tank inlet valve) is on, the rung turns Mix_PumpOut (Mix_Tank outlet pump: transfers to Supply_Tank) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Mix_Step,4) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 4. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Run is on.
  3. XIC(Supply_Inlet) Examine If Closed asks: true when Supply_Inlet is on.
  4. OTE(Mix_PumpOut) Output Energize does: turns Mix_PumpOut on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 7
rungs.comment: START A BATCH: the tank is empty (step 0), or a transfer has just ended with room left (step 4, inlet closed, below 80 %), and both totes have product. The batch tops the tank up to HI. One percent of level is 20 units, one pulse of the flowmeter, so the room to HI is 90 − Mix_Level pulses; the water dose is the recipe share of that room, and the syrup fills the rest. What was left in the tank is already at the recipe, so the topped-up batch is too
rungs.words: When Mix_Run (The mix kitchen is running (its own seal-in)) is on, either (Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 0) or (Mix_Step equals 4, Supply_Inlet (Supply_Tank inlet valve) is off and Mix_Level (Mix_Tank level, 0-100 %) is less than 80), Water_Low (Supply_A (water tote) at its low switch) is off and Conc_Low (Supply_B (syrup tote) at its low switch) is off, the rung computes Dose_Pre (Water dose for this batch, in flowmeter pulses) = (90-Mix_Level)*Mix_Ratio/100, resets Dose_A (Water dose: flowmeter A pulses) and puts 1 into Mix_Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Mix_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. EQU(Mix_Step,0) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
    Path 2
    1. EQU(Mix_Step,4) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 4. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. XIO(Supply_Inlet) Examine If Open asks: true when Supply_Inlet is off.
    3. LES(Mix_Level,80) Less Than asks: true when Mix_Level is less than 80.
  3. XIO(Water_Low) Examine If Open asks: true when Water_Low is off.
  4. XIO(Conc_Low) Examine If Open asks: true when Conc_Low is off.
  5. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. CPT(Dose_Pre,(90-Mix_Level)*Mix_Ratio/100) Compute does: computes Dose_Pre = (90-Mix_Level)*Mix_Ratio/100.
    Path 2
    1. RES(Dose_A) Reset does: resets Dose_A. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 3
    1. MOV(1,Mix_Step) Move does: puts 1 into Mix_Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Mix_Step = 0, to 1); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 8
rungs.comment: PUMP A in step 1

pred.q: Mix_Run is off and Mix_Step is 1. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Mix_PumpA is off. It stops at XIC(Mix_Run).

rungs.words: When Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 1 and Mix_Run (The mix kitchen is running (its own seal-in)) is on, the rung turns Mix_PumpA (Mix_Tank pump A: water) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Mix_Step,1) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 1. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Run is on.
  3. OTE(Mix_PumpA) Output Energize does: turns Mix_PumpA on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 9
rungs.comment: DOSE WATER: count flowmeter A, one pulse per 20 units, to the dose worked out above
rungs.words: When Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 1 and Mix_FlowA (Mix_Tank flowmeter A: one pulse per 20 units) is on, the rung counts Dose_A (Water dose: flowmeter A pulses) up by one (preset Dose_Pre (Water dose for this batch, in flowmeter pulses)).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Mix_Step,1) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 1. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_FlowA) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_FlowA is on.
  3. CTU(Dose_A,Dose_Pre,0) Count Up does: counts Dose_A up by one (preset Dose_Pre). It counts false-to-true transitions of the rung, not scans; .DN is on once the count reaches the preset.

pats.t: A counter: one count per false-to-true.
pats.why: Dose_A counts transitions of the rung, not scans, so a part that sits in front of an eye for a second counts once.
pats.think: a clicker at a door: one click per person coming in, however slowly they walk through.
pats.watch: A counter keeps its count until a RES. If the count should start again at each batch, something has to reset it.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 10
rungs.comment: The water is in: on to the syrup

pred.q: Dose_A.DN is on and Mix_Step is 1. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Mix_Step is written.

rungs.words: When Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 1 and Dose_A.DN (the done bit of Dose_A: Water dose: flowmeter A pulses) is on, the rung puts 2 into Mix_Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Mix_Step,1) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 1. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Dose_A.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Dose_A.DN is on.
  3. MOV(2,Mix_Step) Move does: puts 2 into Mix_Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Mix_Step = 1, to 2); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 11
rungs.comment: PUMP B in step 2, never past HI
rungs.words: When Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 2, Mix_Run (The mix kitchen is running (its own seal-in)) is on and Mix_Hi (Mix_Tank HI probe (90 %)) is off, the rung turns Mix_PumpB (Mix_Tank pump B: syrup) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Mix_Step,2) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 2. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Run is on.
  3. XIO(Mix_Hi) Examine If Open asks: true when Mix_Hi is off.
  4. OTE(Mix_PumpB) Output Energize does: turns Mix_PumpB on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 12
rungs.comment: SYRUP TO HI: the HI probe ends the top-up

pred.q: Mix_Hi is off and Mix_Step is 1. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Mix_Step is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at EQU(Mix_Step,2).

rungs.words: When Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 2 and Mix_Hi (Mix_Tank HI probe (90 %)) is on, the rung puts 3 into Mix_Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Mix_Step,2) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 2. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_Hi) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Hi is on.
  3. MOV(3,Mix_Step) Move does: puts 3 into Mix_Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Mix_Step = 2, to 3); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 13
rungs.comment: MIXER: while the batch heats and mixes, and while it waits and transfers, only with the impeller covered
rungs.words: When either (Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 3) or (Mix_Step equals 4), Mix_Lo (Mix_Tank LO probe (15 %)) is on and Mix_Run (The mix kitchen is running (its own seal-in)) is on, the rung turns Mix_Mixer (Mix_Tank mixer) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. EQU(Mix_Step,3) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
    Path 2
    1. EQU(Mix_Step,4) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 4. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_Lo) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Lo is on.
  3. XIC(Mix_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Run is on.
  4. OTE(Mix_Mixer) Output Energize does: turns Mix_Mixer on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 14
rungs.comment: HEAT ON under the band, only with the element covered

pred.q: Mix_Lo is on, Mix_Step is 3, Mix_Temp is 12 and Mix_Lo_T is 23. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Mix_Heat latches on.

rungs.words: When Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 3, Mix_Lo (Mix_Tank LO probe (15 %)) is on and Mix_Temp (Mix_Tank temperature, °F) is less than Mix_Lo_T (Bottom of the heater band: 2 °F under Mix_Target_T), the rung latches Mix_Heat (Heater wanted (latched under the band, unlatched at the setpoint)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Mix_Step,3) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_Lo) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Lo is on.
  3. LES(Mix_Temp,Mix_Lo_T) Less Than asks: true when Mix_Temp is less than Mix_Lo_T.
  4. OTL(Mix_Heat) Output Latch does: latches Mix_Heat on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Mix_Heat stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 15
rungs.comment: HEAT OFF at the setpoint, if LO uncovers, or out of step 3
rungs.words: When either (Mix_Temp (Mix_Tank temperature, °F) is at least Mix_Target_T (Batch temperature, °F: the setpoint on Tank_HMI (TEMP page))), (Mix_Lo (Mix_Tank LO probe (15 %)) is off) or (Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) is not 3), the rung unlatches Mix_Heat (Heater wanted (latched under the band, unlatched at the setpoint)).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. GEQ(Mix_Temp,Mix_Target_T) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Mix_Temp is at least Mix_Target_T.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Mix_Lo) Examine If Open asks: true when Mix_Lo is off.
    Path 3
    1. NEQ(Mix_Step,3) Not Equal asks: true when Mix_Step is not 3.
  2. OTU(Mix_Heat) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Mix_Heat. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Mix_Heat when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 16
rungs.comment: HEATER: wanted, kitchen running, and the high-limit thermostat not made

pred.q: Mix_Heat is off, Mix_Run is on and Mix_Thermostat is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Mix_Heater is off. It stops at XIC(Mix_Heat).

rungs.words: When Mix_Heat (Heater wanted (latched under the band, unlatched at the setpoint)) is on, Mix_Run (The mix kitchen is running (its own seal-in)) is on and Mix_Thermostat (Mix_Tank high-limit thermostat (180 °F)) is off, the rung turns Mix_Heater (Mix_Tank heater) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Mix_Heat) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Heat is on.
  2. XIC(Mix_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Run is on.
  3. XIO(Mix_Thermostat) Examine If Open asks: true when Mix_Thermostat is off.
  4. OTE(Mix_Heater) Output Energize does: turns Mix_Heater on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 17
rungs.comment: MIX TIME counts once the batch is up to temperature with the mixer running
rungs.words: When Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 3, Mix_Mixer (Mix_Tank mixer) is on and Mix_Temp (Mix_Tank temperature, °F) is at least Mix_Lo_T (Bottom of the heater band: 2 °F under Mix_Target_T), the rung runs the timer Mix_Timer (Mixing time at temperature) toward Mix_Ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Mix_Step,3) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_Mixer) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Mixer is on.
  3. GEQ(Mix_Temp,Mix_Lo_T) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Mix_Temp is at least Mix_Lo_T.
  4. TON(Mix_Timer,Mix_Ms,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Mix_Timer toward Mix_Ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Mix_Timer counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 18
rungs.comment: BATCH READY

pred.q: Mix_Timer.DN is on and Mix_Step is 3. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Mix_Step is written.

rungs.words: When Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 3 and Mix_Timer.DN (the done bit of Mix_Timer: Mixing time at temperature) is on, the rung puts 4 into Mix_Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Mix_Step,3) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_Timer.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Timer.DN is on.
  3. MOV(4,Mix_Step) Move does: puts 4 into Mix_Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Mix_Step = 3, to 4); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 19
rungs.comment: EMPTY: LO uncovered for 2 s while transferring (the pump takes the heel below the probe)
rungs.words: When Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer) equals 4 and Mix_Lo (Mix_Tank LO probe (15 %)) is off, the rung runs the timer Mix_Empty_T (LO uncovered this long: the tank is empty) toward 2000 ms (2 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Mix_Step,4) Equal asks: true when Mix_Step equals 4. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIO(Mix_Lo) Examine If Open asks: true when Mix_Lo is off.
  3. TON(Mix_Empty_T,2000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Mix_Empty_T toward 2000 ms (2 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Mix_Empty_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 20
rungs.comment: Back to step 0: the next batch starts at once, so one is ready before Supply_Tank calls again

pred.q: Mix_Empty_T.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Mix_Step is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIC(Mix_Empty_T.DN).

rungs.words: When Mix_Empty_T.DN (the done bit of Mix_Empty_T: LO uncovered this long: the tank is empty) is on, the rung puts 0 into Mix_Step (Kitchen sequence: 0 empty, 1 dose water, 2 syrup to HI, 3 heat and mix, 4 ready / transfer).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Mix_Empty_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Empty_T.DN is on.
  2. MOV(0,Mix_Step) Move does: puts 0 into Mix_Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 21
rungs.comment: CO2, only for a recipe that takes it (Mix_Carb, from the RECIPE page; soda and sparkling water do, juice, water and milk do not) and only with the carbonation key on the console turned to ON (Carb_Key; Tank_HMI shows a yellow CARBONATION OFF strip until it is): hold the carbonator between 19 and 22 psi. At 38 °F that dissolves 3.5 to 3.8 volumes of CO2 in the soda going through. Under 19 psi the valve opens and seals itself in; at 22 it drops out and stays shut until the pressure falls back under 19. Every 100 units of soda going through takes about 3 psi of CO2 with it
rungs.words: When either (Carb_Press (Carbonator tank pressure, psi) is less than 19) or (Carb_CO2 (Carbonator CO2 inlet valve) is on), Carb_Press is less than 22, Mix_Run (The mix kitchen is running (its own seal-in)) is on, Mix_Carb (The recipe takes CO2 (1 for soda; set by the RECIPE page on Tank_HMI). The carbonator's CO2 valve only works while it is 1: juice, water and milk go through still) is on and Carb_Key (The carbonation key on the console, 1 turned to ON: the kitchen may carbonate) is on, the rung turns Carb_CO2 on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. LES(Carb_Press,19) Less Than asks: true when Carb_Press is less than 19.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Carb_CO2) Examine If Closed asks: true when Carb_CO2 is on.
  2. LES(Carb_Press,22) Less Than asks: true when Carb_Press is less than 22.
  3. XIC(Mix_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Run is on.
  4. XIC(Mix_Carb) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_Carb is on.
  5. XIC(Carb_Key) Examine If Closed asks: true when Carb_Key is on.
  6. OTE(Carb_CO2) Output Energize does: turns Carb_CO2 on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Carb_CO2 on, and Carb_CO2’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.

rungs.head: S13_Mix · Rung 22
rungs.comment: The amber CO2 lamp beside the key: carbonation is enabled. Off, and a soda batch goes to Supply_Tank still; the kitchen's screen says so in yellow

pred.q: Carb_Key is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Carb_Lamp is on.

rungs.words: When Carb_Key (The carbonation key on the console, 1 turned to ON: the kitchen may carbonate) is on, the rung turns Carb_Lamp (The amber CO2 lamp beside the key: carbonation enabled) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Carb_Key) Examine If Closed asks: true when Carb_Key is on.
  2. OTE(Carb_Lamp) Output Energize does: turns Carb_Lamp on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
